senses.gloss: resting place, esp. a structure next to or over a tomb. Ohol. VII, 1 נ׳ אטומה a solid tomb-structure (to which there is no access).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Shekalim 2:5">Shek. II, 5</cite> <he>מותר המת בונין לו נ׳ וכ׳</he> from what is left over of the appropriation for funeral expenses, we build a monument &c.; (<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 82:10">Gen. R. s. 82</cite> <cite ref="B00753"><he>בַּיִת</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Tosefta Eiruvin 6:4">Tosef. Erub. VI</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Eiruvin 5:4">V</cite>), 4, sq.; <cite ref="Eruvin 55b:10">Erub. 55ᵇ</cite> (contrad. to <he>קבר</he>).—Pl. <he>נְפָשׁוֹת</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Eruvin 5:1">Ib. V, 1</cite> <he>נ׳</he> sepulchres (containing a place of shelter).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 2:5:1">Y. Shek. II, 47ᵃ</cite> top; Gen. R. l. c. <he>אין עושין נ׳ וכ׳</he> no monuments need be put up for the righteous, v. <cite ref="G00470"><he>זִכָּרוֹן</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Ohalot 17:4">Tosef. Ohol. XVII, 4</cite> <he>חוקת נ׳ שבא״י וכ׳</he> the presumption in the case of sepulchres in Palestine is that they are levitically clean, except those marked.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 4:6">B. Mets. IV, 6</cite> <he>שאינו אלא נ׳ רעה</he> for it (the refusal of a coin on the ground of a slight abrasion) proves merely a malevolent soul (illiberality in dealing); <cite ref="Bava Metzia 52b:10">ib. 52ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="S00204"><he>קְהֵי</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 14:10">Gen. R. s. 14</cite> (names of the soul) <he>נ׳ רוח וכ׳</he>.
Ib. נ׳ זו הדם nefesh means blood (life).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 14:10">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 2:7">Gen. II, 7</cite>, a.
VII, 22) כאן הוא עושה נשמה נ׳ וכ׳ here the text calls the soul (נשמה) nefesh, and there, ruaḥ (spirit); ib. s. 32.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5">Snh. IV, 5</cite> <he>נ׳ אחת</he> one (person’s) life.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 3:1:2">Y. Taan. III, beg. 66ᵇ</cite> <he>מכיון שנתנו ב״ד נַפְשָׁן וכ׳</he> as soon as the court has declared its will to do a thing.
Nidd. 65ᵇ, a. fr. בעל נ׳ one who is master over his desire, a conscientious man.—

<cite ref="Berakhot 44b:9">Ber. 44ᵇ</cite> <he>כל נ׳ משיב את הנ׳</he> all life (animal food) restores life; <he>וכל קרוב לנ׳ וכ׳</he> and what is nearest life (the neck which contains the jugular vein) &c.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 5:7:5">Y. Keth. V, 30ᵇ</cite> top <he>דברים שהן קיום נ׳</he> things required for sustaining life.

<cite ref="Yoma 74b:10">Yoma 74ᵇ</cite> <he>אבידת נ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="A00131"><he>אֲבֵירָה</he></cite>; a. v. fr.—<he>דחה נ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="D00397"><he>דָּחָה</he></cite>.—Sifra M’tsorʿa, Zab., Par. 3, ch. VI <he>ואם נַפְשְׁךָ לומר וכ׳</he> (= <he>ואיבעית אימא</he>, v. <cite ref="B01037"><he>בְּעֵי</he></cite>) or if you prefer (another argument); <cite ref="Chullin 78b">Ḥull. 78ᵇ</cite> bot.

<cite ref="Chullin 78b:12">Ib.</cite> <he>מה ואם נפשך לומר</he> why should you prefer another argument?, i.e. what objection can there be to the argument offered before?—(<cite ref="M00000"><he>מ</he></cite>)<he>מה נפשך</he>, v. <cite ref="M00340"><he>מָה</he></cite>.—
Ḥull. IV, 7 (77ᵃ) נ׳ היפה one not fastidious.—
B. Bath. 89ᵃ נ׳ מאזנים the opening in which the tongue of scales rests (agina).—Pl. as ab. דיני נ׳, v. דִּין II. Snh. l. c. עדי נ׳ witnesses in capital cases.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 8:6">Yoma VIII, 6</cite> <he>ספק נ׳</he> the possibility of danger to human life; <cite ref="Shabbat 129a:21">Sabb. 129ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.
